function.arguments: {"beats":[{"title":"They set the scene at the window","note":"Opens on stillness: someone has been watching for an hour and the household has not registered it. Sets up the waiting the rest of the draft turns on.","quote":"She had been standing at the window for an hour before anyone noticed."},{"title":"They let the kettle go cold","note":"A small domestic failure that stands for the whole household stalling. Paid off when the kettle is filled at the end.","quote":"The kettle went cold on the counter, and nobody moved to fill it again."},{"title":"They introduce the father and his distrust of the thermostat","note":"Introduces the thermostat the regulation passage depends on and the father who does not believe in it.","quote":"Her father had installed the thermostat himself the winter before, and he never trusted it."},{"title":"They say what the thermostat can and cannot know","note":"The central metaphor: perfect regulation of one measurement, blind to the rest of the house.","quote":"It kept a single promise, to hold the hallway at nineteen degrees, and it kept that promise with total loyalty and no understanding."},{"title":"They have the brother answer the telephone","note":"Breaks the waiting. The brother is the one who has stopped pretending, which the first section only hinted at.","quote":"When the telephone finally rang, it was her brother who crossed the room, because he was the only one who had stopped pretending not to wait."},{"title":"They close on the kettle being filled","note":"Pays off the cold kettle from the opening: action replaces waiting.","quote":"Nobody had noticed that either, and she crossed the kitchen and filled it, because it was the one thing in the room that she knew how to do."}]}
